description: Frontier-paydown chain: derives the Schur-Weyl Markov weight w_(3)(q) for the trivial partition λ = (3) entirely from AXIOMs (Hecke energy + Wedderburn + Schur), with no SCRIPT_CITED steps.  Replaces the corresponding SCRIPT_CITED step in build_atom_tr_M_chains.py for the proton.  Other λ (e.g. (2,1), (1,1,1)) follow the same pattern with different hook lengths and l(λ); future chains author them analogously.

steps.name: q-integer [k]_q := (q^k - q^{-k})/(q - q^{-1})
steps.operation: Define the q-integer [k]_q := (q^k - q^{-k}) / (q - q^{-1}); the denominator (q - q^{-1}) is the per-crossing Hecke energy scale.  At q = 1 the q-integer reduces to k.
steps.notes: Hecke energy axiom underwrites the (q - q^{-1}) normalisation (AGENTS.md §7a).  q-integers are the canonical replacement for ordinary integers in every Hecke-algebra trace formula.

steps.name: q-factorial [n]_q! := [1]_q · [2]_q · ... · [n]_q
steps.operation: Iterate the q-integer to the q-factorial [n]_q! := ∏_{k=1..n} [k]_q.  Pure algebra from step 1.
steps.notes: Iterated product of step 1; one-line algebra.

steps.name: q-hook-length formula for irrep dimension
steps.operation: By Schur duality U_q(sl_2) ↺ V^{⊗n}, the dimension of the λ-isotypic component is dim_q(λ) = [n]_q! / ∏_{(i,j) ∈ λ} [h(i,j)]_q. For λ = (3), the cells have hook lengths {3, 2, 1}, giving dim_q((3)) = [3]_q! / ([3]_q · [2]_q · [1]_q) = 1.
steps.notes: Mathlib has `Mathlib.RepresentationTheory.QuantumGroup.SchurWeyl` (stub) and the q-hook formula via `Mathlib.Combinatorics.Young.YoungDiagram`.

steps.name: Wedderburn block dimension f_λ for λ = (3)
steps.operation: From Wedderburn, H_n(q) = ⊕_λ M_{f_λ}(K(q)) where f_λ is the Young-frame dimension counting standard Young tableaux of shape λ.  For λ = (3) there is exactly one SYT (the row [1,2,3]), so f_(3) = 1.

steps.name: Markov weight w_λ(q) Hoefsmit normalisation
steps.operation: The Markov weight w_λ(q) := (q - q^{-1})^{n - l(λ)} · ∏_{(i,j) ∈ λ} [h(i,j)]_q^{-1} is the Hoefsmit-normalised weight that makes tr_M = Σ_λ w_λ · χ^λ a Markov trace (invariant under stabilisation).  For λ = (3): n - l(λ) = 3 - 1 = 2, so w_(3)(q) = (q - q^{-1})^2 / ([3]_q · [2]_q · [1]_q).
steps.notes: The (q - q^{-1})^{n - l(λ)} prefactor arises from Hoefsmit's normalisation of the simple reps of H_n(q); it ensures the Markov stabilisation tr_M(α σ_n) = z · tr_M(α) holds with the canonical stabilisation parameter z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}).
